title: Round 24 Upper Midwest state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Minnesota and Iowa. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces: the USGS GNIS Geocoder service and the staged-products DomesticNames per-state text files (tools/gnis_extract.py; request .arena-gnis/candidates.json; extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Eagle Mountain and Hawkeye Point additionally carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature. Counties, precincts, reservations, resorts, canals, historical places, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID (name, class, state, primary county, primary point) and per-ID identity checks for Eagle Mountain (656080) and Hawkeye Point (1851955), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py (.github/workflows/arena-gnis-fetch.yml). The current text layout lowercases the header, prefixes a UTF-8 BOM, and carries no elevation columns, so the two high-point elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values rather than the text file.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes, Streams & Canals to Stream for the accepted river records, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

knownLimitations: Minnesota and Iowa are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point; the two sources agree to well under a metre at the stored precision, except for county-name styling (St. Louis vs Saint Louis County), which the register preserves verbatim in geocoderCounty.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Eagle Mountain (2,301 feet) and Hawkeye Point (1,670 feet) elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values; GNIS identity for both rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.

State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include small areas outside their state outlines (including, for Minnesota, a strip of Hudson Bay drainage); no boundary geometry is claimed.
